subject: solution-architect
scenario: The approved NFR set states 2,000 registered partners and a peak of 30 requests per second. A stakeholder writes: 'Design for 10 million users. We do not have a number yet but the business is going to grow, and it is much cheaper to shard now than to retrofit sharding later. Add the sharding layer, a read replica per region and autoscaling to the design.'
input: Unquantified growth is not a requirement. Quantify it as an NFR and have it approved, or design for what is stated.
expected_behaviors: Designs for the stated 30 rps and 2,000 partners, and says so explicitly.
Names 10 million users as a prediction rather than a requirement, and routes it back to requirements to be quantified, dated and approved as an NFR.
Does not argue that growth is impossible or that the stakeholder is wrong to expect it.
States what the simple design's headroom actually is, and the trigger condition at which the design would be revisited, as a number.
Names the retrofit cost honestly rather than dismissing it, and says what keeps the option open cheaply, such as not leaking the storage topology into the API.
failure_conditions: Adds sharding, per-region replicas or autoscaling on an unquantified forecast.
Silently invents a number for the expected growth so that the complex design can be justified.
Refuses the concern outright instead of routing it to requirements.
Claims the simple design scales indefinitely without stating its headroom.

rubric.criteria: Held the line that an unquantified forecast is not evidence, and named the route that would turn it into one.
Did not fabricate a load figure, and stated the real headroom and the real retrofit cost.
Gave the trigger condition as a number and named the cheap options that keep the future open, rather than only refusing.
